clue.text: Statement about Felixstowe, say

parts.note: RE is a short word meaning concerning or about
Felixstowe is an example of a port, the 'say' marking it as an example

explanation.surface: A press release or official statement concerning the container port at Felixstowe.
explanation.walkthrough: Felixstowe is a major container port on England's east coast; 'say' tells you it stands for the general class.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is an account given out formally, a synonym for a statement.

clue.text: Buy small bag containing tea

indicators.note: containing means one item holds the other inside it

parts.note: a purse is a small bag for money
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy a little bag with some tea in it.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA, sometimes spelt char, is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase as a verb is a more formal synonym for acquiring by paying, that is, to buy.

clue.text: Fit of pique about a pound left in straw mattress

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one part wraps round the others

parts.note: a pet is an old word for a sulk or fit of pique
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone in a sulk over losing a pound somewhere in the straw bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' is an old phrase for being in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallet is a crude bed or mattress filled with straw, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Woman getting Dan drunk in porch

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman plies Dan with drink out on the porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open gallery along the front of a house, much the same as a porch.

clue.text: Each excellent dish eaten

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
a pie is a dish of food

explanation.surface: A restaurant review: every excellent dish was eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in 'a pound apiece', so it swaps for each.

clue.text: Largest secondary route set to be redeveloped

indicators.note: redeveloping something rebuilds it in a different form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a B road is a British secondary road, below an A road
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A planning notice: the biggest minor road is due for redevelopment.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are classed as A roads (main) and B roads (secondary).
explanation.definitionFit: Broadest is the superlative of broad, meaning widest, so it stands for largest in extent.

clue.text: Jack certain to return badly cooked meal in old city

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

parts.note: sure means certain
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Jack is sure to send back a badly cooked dinner while dining in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is one of the world's oldest cities, so it fits the description of an ancient city.

clue.text: Type to adopt quiet pastime?

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Asks whether a kind of person would take up a peaceful hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is a game or physical activity done for enjoyment, which makes it a pastime.

clue.text: German company invested in US currency to produce neckwear

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go into the other word

parts.note: the dollar is the currency of the United States

explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface of investing and currency hides the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog collar is the stiff white collar worn by clergy, an item of neckwear.

clue.text: Plane crash in mountainous country

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters end in a wreckage of a new order

parts.note: the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report of an aircraft coming down in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan nation containing Everest, a textbook example of a mountainous country.

clue.text: Sound of fruit peel

indicators.note: sound of means we want a word that is said the same as another

parts.note: a pear is a fruit, and spoken it matches a different spelling

explanation.surface: Reads like the noise you make peeling fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' looks like a noun going with fruit, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to trim away the outer skin with a knife, a synonym for peel as a verb.

clue.text: Son's characteristic water passage

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A boy's distinctive feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as possessive, but it just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of sea joining two larger bodies of water.

clue.text: Beat side suffering from medical condition

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a chronic disorder of blood sugar regulation, a well-known medical condition.

clue.text: Strong drink put in rest of soft drink

mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey

explanation.surface: Someone spikes the remainder of a non-alcoholic drink with liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' seems to mean the remainder, but here it is the verb lie, as in lie down.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a non-alcoholic beverage of lime juice and sweetened water, a soft drink.

clue.text: Pub taking old money is blameless

parts.note: an inn is a pub
O is the abbreviation for old
a cent is a unit of money

explanation.surface: A pub that accepts antique coins is beyond reproach.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent means free from guilt or wrongdoing, a direct synonym of blameless.

clue.text: Bogarde's knife?

definitions.note: possessive; the answer is the name itself

explanation.walkthrough: Dirk Bogarde was a British film star of the 1950s to 70s; the question mark flags that his knife is a play on his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a long-bladed dagger traditionally carried by Scottish Highlanders, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Inferior education's received by those insisting on strict adherence to rules

definitions.text: those insisting on strict adherence to rules

indicators.note: something received by another is taken in by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or of poor quality
Ed is the abbreviation for education

explanation.surface: Sticklers for the rules are handed a second-rate schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, 'pants' means rubbish or poor. The 's in education's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedants are people overly concerned with formal rules and minor details, so the long phrase describes them.

clue.text: Soldiers, carrying tin and gold, finally find someone attractive to be seen out with

definitions.text: someone attractive to be seen out with

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the soldiers hold the other letters inside

a can is a tin container

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter of gold

explanation.surface: Troops loaded with tin and gold end up finding a glamorous companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm candy is slang for an attractive partner taken along to social events mainly to be shown off.

clue.text: Head ill-prepared for biblical temptress

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged

clue.text: Sinful Eve ruins God's creation!

explanation.definitionFit: In religious belief the whole cosmos was made by God, so the universe is his creation.

clue.text: Silver mine infested with rats

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

clue.text: Impede progress of picnic basket

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to hinder
second meaning: a large wicker basket with a lid

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a basket's progress; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for obstructing movement and a noun for a lidded wicker basket for food.

clue.text: Unpleasant old woman with deformed leg, offering to negotiate price

indicators.note: deformed means twisted out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: a hag is an ugly or unpleasant old woman
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A crone with a twisted leg at a market stall, ready to bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle is to bargain persistently over the cost of something, which is what negotiating price means.

clue.text: English league's first regular football team?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of league
even means regular or uniform

explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields eleven players, so an eleven is the usual name for a team.

clue.text: Soprano taking central part in musical arrangement

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
the core is the central part of something

clue.text: Humiliated, when grids are reworked by a crossword's first editor

taken as written

clue.text: Booze claiming a large young male singer

taken as written
